thread:
Ian: Quick sync: planning a multi-region drain + failover bench that mixes synthetic steady-state load with replayed production traces. Goal: quantify tail when KV hit drops and kernel fallback triggers (esp. p95/p99 under failover). Thoughts on methodology?
Sana: +1. For apples-to-apples we should pin: model version, quantization, and the kernel selection logic. Also keep batcher settings identical across regions and disable any autoscaler.
Ian: Agreed. Draft command for replay harness (example):
```
./replay_harness --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-03/choose_first100k.json --rate 2000 --region us-east-1 --preserve-kv=true \
  --force-kernel=kernel_v2 --batch-ms=8 --batch-token-cap=2048 --seq-dist=prod --pin-gpu=true
```
This preserves KV behavior and forces a kernel. We'll run same command in us-west-2 with identical flags.
Chen: For the KV hit curve test we should sweep prewarm window and TTL, measure kv_hit_rate + p50/p95/p99 latencies and token throughput. Example perf line from a small run:
`kv_hit_rate=0.87 p50=34ms p95=112ms p99=420ms tokens/s=12k kernel=kernel_v2 batch_ms=8`
Mike: We should normalize tails by tokens-per-second to account for load differences. Also capture 'kernel-switch count' per minute (how often runtime falls back to slower kernels) and correlate with tail spikes.
Ian: Good call. How do we trigger failover? My plan: 1) run steady-state replay in both regions; 2) initiate simulated drain on primary (us-east) by removing nodes from LB; 3) route traffic to secondary (us-west) and measure:
- cold model activations (new KV misses)
- KV decay curve over time
- kernel-switch rate and p99
Sana: Don't forget to disable node autoscaler and leader election reshuffles. If we let autoscaler add capacity mid-test we won't get consistent tails. Also pin instance types (same GPU gen) and disable dynamic kernel autotuner.
replay-bot: started replay job 1768154321-01 on us-west-2 (trace=first100k, rate=2000, preserve_kv=true)
Chen: I'll run the KV sweep first thing. Plan: run TTLs=[30s,90s,300s,900s], prewarm-rates=[0,0.25,0.5,1.0], measure 10m windows. Expect p99 to jump when kv_hit_rate < ~0.6 and kernel falls back.
Mike: Also collect profiler stacks every 30s during the drain window (sampled), like:
```
perf_sample --pid <runtime_pid> --interval 30s --duration 600s > drain-1768154321.perf
```
We need to annotate traces with region and kernel metadata.
Ian: Action items: Chen run KV sweeps (start now), Mike add kernel-switch metric + profiler hooks, Sana prepare isolated infra (disable autoscale + pin GPUs), I'll orchestrate the drain and collect dashboards. We'll reconvene in 2h with initial numbers. :thumbsup:
Mike: on it. :eyes:
Sana: I'll also create a little dashboard comparing kv_hit_rate -> p99 over time and a histogram of kernel-switches.
Chen: Starting first sweep now, posting logs to /runs/drainbench/1768154321. Will include a short summary when done.
Mike: Thanks — ping when the first run completes so I can pull profiler samples.
Ian: Perfect. If we see large perf regressions we'll isolate by running with `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=baseline` vs `=kernel_v2` to see delta. Keep all artifacts in run dir.
